scope: independent root verification of the Z[x] quotient theorem, the mixed-integral consequence, the exact circularity in arXiv:2007.15000v3, and the missing synchronization in arXiv:1706.08394v7

mathematical_audit.automorphism: The finite geometric operator identity (1+D) sum_j (-D)^j P=P proves that P -> S_P is an integral automorphism, with no denominator hypothesis.
mathematical_audit.quotient: Endpoint evaluation after this automorphism is onto Z^2. Its kernel is exactly x(x-1)Z[x] in S-coordinates, hence (1+D)(x(x-1)Z[x]) in P-coordinates.
mathematical_audit.degree_one_section: For arbitrary integers A,C, P=A+(A-C)x has S=C+(A-C)x and endpoints (A,C).
mathematical_audit.integral_gauge: Every higher-degree kernel element gives d(e^x x(x-1)R)/dx and integrates to zero on [0,1]. It changes no integer linear form.
mathematical_audit.certificate_equivalence: The unrestricted mixed-polynomial decay condition is exactly the standard integer-linear-form condition for e+pi; the identity alone does not prove that condition.
mathematical_audit.claimed_sum_proof: Under A+Be+C*pi=0, the claimed nonzero sine is sin(Be+A)=sin(-C*pi)=0. Lemma 7.2 invokes Lemma 6.2(ii), which asserts the same forbidden integer relation, so the argument is circular.
mathematical_audit.independent_inequality_failure: For k=m=1,r=1, rational bounds on e and pi give |e+1-3*pi/2|<1 while ||e-1|-3*pi/2|>2.9, reversing the purported inequality in equation (6.7).
mathematical_audit.claimed_product_proof: The required fixed-window hit by a pi convergent denominator is not established. The supporting lemma assumes unproved partial-quotient growth, makes an invalid implication from b_m=o(m), and writes unsupported multiplicative identities for unrelated continuants.

PROVED: all-degree integral automorphism and endpoint quotient
degree-one section and exact higher-degree zero-integral gauge
equivalence of the unrestricted mixed-polynomial condition with the original irrationality criterion
the cited direct proof does not establish linear independence
the cited product proof does not establish its synchronization lemma
